original_value: The metaheuristic genetic algorithm (GA) is based on the natural selection process that falls under the umbrella category of evolutionary algorithms (EA). Genetic algorithms are typically utilized for generating high-quality solutions for search and optimization problems by depending on bio-oriented operators such as selection, crossover, and mutation. However, the GA still suffers from some downsides and needs to be improved so as to attain greater control of exploitation and exploration concerning creating a new population and randomness involvement happening in the population at the solution initialization. Furthermore, the mutation is imposed upon the new chromosomes and hence prevents the achievement of an optimal solution. Therefore, this study presents a new GA that is centered on the natural selection theory and it aims to improve the control of exploitation and exploration. The proposed algorithm is called genetic algorithm based on natural selection theory (GABONST). Two assessments of the GABONST are carried out via (i) application of fifteen renowned benchmark test functions and the comparison of the results with the conventional GA, enhanced ameliorated teaching learning-based optimization (EATLBO), Bat and Bee algorithms. (ii) Apply the GABONST in language identification (LID) through integrating the GABONST with extreme learning machine (ELM) and named (GABONST-ELM). The ELM is considered as one of the most useful learning models for carrying out classifications and regression analysis. The generation of results is carried out grounded upon the LID dataset, which is derived from eight separate languages. The GABONST algorithm has the capability of producing good quality solutions and it also has better control of the exploitation and exploration as compared to the conventional GA, EATLBO, Bat, and Bee algorithms in terms of the statistical assessment. Additionally, the obtained results indicate that (GABONST-ELM)-LID has an effective performance with accuracy reaching up to 99.38%.

result.paraphrase: The genetic algorithm (GA), a metaheuristic grounded in natural selection, belongs to the broader family of evolutionary algorithms (EA). It is commonly used to produce high-quality solutions for search and optimization tasks through bio-inspired operators such as selection, crossover, and mutation. Even so, GA has shortcomings and requires improvement to better regulate exploitation and exploration during new-population creation, as well as the randomness involved when initializing the population. In addition, mutation is applied to the newly formed chromosomes, which hinders reaching an optimal solution. To address this, the study introduces a new GA based on natural selection theory, designed to improve control over exploitation and exploration. This method is named genetic algorithm based on natural selection theory (GABONST). The GABONST is evaluated in two ways: first, by applying it to fifteen well-known benchmark test functions and comparing its results with conventional GA, enhanced ameliorated teaching learning-based optimization (EATLBO), Bat, and Bee algorithms; second, by using it for language identification (LID) through integration with extreme learning machine (ELM), termed GABONST-ELM. ELM is regarded as one of the most effective learning models for classification and regression. Results are generated using the LID dataset, which consists of eight different languages. Statistically, GABONST is capable of generating high-quality solutions and provides better exploitation-exploration control than conventional GA, EATLBO, Bat, and Bee algorithms. Moreover, the findings show that (GABONST-ELM)-LID performs effectively, achieving accuracy of up to 99.38%.
